name: Quantization runtime cost: dequant, scale unpacking, and batch crossover
arithmetic_intensity: Quantization changes the bytes-per-flop ratio of every weight GEMM by the compression factor: a 4-bit weight format cuts weight bytes 4x versus bf16, so decode GEMM AI goes from ~B to ~4B flop/byte and the effective ridge crossing batch drops by roughly the compression factor. The overhead is that unpacking scales and converting to a compute-representable form costs real work and real memory traffic. The question that matters for serving is when quantized kernels stop paying: Marlin reports that for 4-bit weights, batches up to 16-32 still get close to the maximum ~4x quantization speedup, with batches up to 64-128 seeing gradually decreasing but still significant acceleration, and up to 2.8x end-to-end integrated with vLLM (arXiv 2408.11743). That crossover is the whole engineering question - below it, quantization is nearly free speedup; above it, the dequant traffic starts to be paid on every step.
scales_with: bits (directly sets the bytes and hence AI)
weight_group_size (smaller groups mean more scales to unpack - more overhead per element)
batch_size (THE crossover knob: AI = bits_compound_factor * B, so the batch at which dequant stops paying is set by bits)
activation_quantization_scheme (per-tensor vs per-channel dynamic quantization adds work)
hardware_native_support (emulated dequant-to-fp16 pays overhead a native path does not)
workarounds: MARLIN-style mixed-precision GEMM: asynchronous memory access, complex task scheduling/pipelining and bespoke quantization support, keeping 4-bit weight traffic bandwidth-bound up to batch 16-32 and useful to 64-128 (arXiv 2408.11743)
Native low-precision tensor-core paths (FP8 / INT8 / FP4 on device) so dequant is fused into the load rather than done in a separate pass
Pre-quantized weights so the format is not re-derived per launch
Fused dequant-into-shared-memory GEMM epilogues rather than a separate dequant kernel
Asymmetric group-wise scale layout that allows vectorized 4-bit loads
notes:
Design consequence: the reason quantization speedups are quoted as 'up to 4x' is that they are batch-conditional, and the condition is a batch number. An engine that quantizes for a latency target (batch 1) gets nearly the full win; an engine that quantizes to serve high concurrency gets a decaying fraction of it, because batching already raised AI and the weight bytes stopped being the binding constraint. Hardware designers should treat 'does it have a native int4/fp8 path' as the decisive question and 'what is the batch crossover of that path' as the second. Also note the asymmetry the Marlin result exposes: a format with no native support is emulated by dequantizing to fp16, which converts a bandwidth win into a bandwidth cost - the dequantized intermediate must be written and re-read, so a '4-bit' model can run slower than bf16 on hardware without a native path. KV-cache quantization is a separate decision recorded under kv_transfer and decode_attention: it does not touch the GEMM ridge at all, it halves the attention and transfer traffic.
